title: Cepheus Weakly Solves Heads-Up Limit Texas Hold’em Poker via CFR⁺ Regret Minimization
whyItMatters: Published in Science, Cepheus became the first nontrivial imperfect-information game played competitively by humans to be essentially weakly solved—computing a near-exact Nash equilibrium across 3.16×10¹⁴ decision points.
summary: Published in Science on January 9, 2015, Michael Bowling, Neil Burch, Michael Johanson, and Oskari Tammelin at the University of Alberta unveiled Cepheus, which essentially weakly solved heads-up limit Texas hold’em poker. Introducing the CFR⁺ (Counterfactual Regret Minimization Plus) algorithm and custom lossless compression across 3.16×10¹⁴ information sets, Cepheus computed a Nash-equilibrium strategy with exploitability below 0.001 big blinds per game—statistically indistinguishable from unbeatable over a human lifetime—and formally proved that the dealer holds a quantifiable first-mover advantage.
technicalHighlights: Introduced CFR⁺, accelerating imperfect-information extensive-form game solving by three orders of magnitude.
Computed a near-exact Nash equilibrium across 3.16×10¹⁴ decision points (11 TB compressed strategy) with exploitability <0.001 bb/hand.
Formally proved the longstanding poker folklore that the dealer position holds a statistically significant strategic advantage.
caveats: Essentially weakly solved heads-up limit hold’em (not no-limit or multiplayer poker); exploitability is mathematically bounded below statistical detectability over a lifetime rather than strictly zero.

scoreRationale.foundational: First human-competitive imperfect-information game solved to mathematical equilibrium, solving a core challenge in computational game theory.
scoreRationale.ripple: CFR⁺ became the algorithmic backbone of superhuman imperfect-information AI (DeepStack, Libratus, Pluribus) and strategic decision systems.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Vol. 347, pp. 145–149) with publicly queryable strategy database.
scoreRationale.velocity: Solved a 10¹⁴-state hidden-information game tree in 68 days of cluster compute.
